1 big thing: All quiet on the Atlantic front
 
Illustration: Natalie Peeples/Axios

This storm season is breaking at least one record: It's the longest the Atlantic has gone in the modern era without a recorded hurricane, Axios New Orleans' Chelsea Brasted reports.

  • That's per meteorologist and hurricane-watcher Michael Lowry, who writes: "None of this is to say that we can't or won't see a week or two before the end of November where a big hurricane breaks through, but for the traditional height of the hurricane season, it doesn't get any better than this."

🌀 This year's hurricane season was expected to be quieter than normal. But experts still predicted eight to 14 named storms and three to six hurricanes.

  • We've had just five named tropical storms so far.

National Weather Service meteorologist Christopher Bannan notes that the satellite era began in 1966, ushering in the modern storm-tracking age.

  • Bannan says we know of two prior years without any Atlantic hurricanes: 1907 and 1914.
A man watches debris flow along a road in Naalehu, Hawaii, on Aug. 17 after Hurricane Lala brought heavy rain and strong winds. Photo: Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images

🌏 Yes, but: The Central Pacific has been notably active, with five named storms (+3 over the 1991–2020 normal) and two major hurricanes (+2).

  • This year's especially powerful El Niño is fueling storm development in the Pacific while hampering it in the Atlantic, University of Tampa environmental studies professor Nicholas Grondin tells Scientific American.

2. 🗳️ Democrats' polling edge
 
Data: New York Times/Siena poll; Chart: Erin Davis/Axios Visuals

Likely voters prefer Democratic candidates over Republicans in their congressional district by nearly 9 percentage points, a new N.Y. Times/Siena University poll finds.

  • That metric is "closely watched by both parties as a leading indicator of political momentum," the Times notes. (Gift link.)

🖼️ The big picture: President Trump's overall approval rating sits at 38%, per the poll.

  • Most voters disapprove of his handling of the economy, the war with Iran, affordability and other major issues.

🐘 The other side: A new Reuters/Ipsos poll finds that Trump's approval rating is up from a record low, hitting 35% from 33% after the Republicans' midterm convention last week.

Reality check: Polls can't fully predict elections, especially given the gerrymandering and map-redrawing efforts in the lead-up to November's midterms that have left few House seats in play.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Via Truth Social

4. ⚾️ 1 fun thing: A softball for the Pope
 
Pope Leo and Ron Onesti in Rome. Photo: Courtesy of Ron Onesti

During a recent visit to the Vatican to meet Pope Leo XIV, Chicagoan Ron Onesti had to dig deep to figure out what to bring as a gift.

  • His choice? A 16-inch softball — a Chicago classic, from a spin on traditional softball, Axios Chicago's Justin Kaufmann reports.

🍕 Onesti tells Axios: "I couldn't bring him a beef. I couldn't bring him a pizza. Giardiniera was already taken."

  • "You know, so not a whole lot left."
